message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.75 (≈$9,801 — within the $10,000 per-order cap, and well under the $20,000 daily cap; buy-only, no cash transfers, no MSFT activity).

**Summary:** Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 9/28/2024, filed 11/1/2024) shows a fundamentally solid, cash-generative business: total net sales of $391,035M (up 2% y/y), operating income of $123,216M (operating margin ~31.5%), net income of $93,736M and diluted EPS of $6.08 — with net income depressed by a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge related to the EC State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7% a year earlier), which is a non-recurring item rather than an operating deterioration. Operating cash flow of $118,254M and a gross margin of 46.2% (up 130bps) confirm the underlying earnings power, and Services revenue grew 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% gross margin, offsetting flat iPhone sales ($201,183M) and an 8% decline in Greater China ($66,952M) — the main soft spot, alongside DOJ/EU DMA antitrust risk flagged in the filing. Today's feed showed only routine intraday noise (a drift from ~$221.8 to ~$220.5 on repeated "little changed" headlines, plus mildly supportive supplier-build notes on iPhone 16), and the news flow was neutral — shares steady around $222 as analysts weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, with holiday-quarter estimates unchanged. With the live quote at $222.70 (bid/ask $222.68/$222.72), I bought a modest starter position of 44 shares at a $222.75 limit — essentially at the market, sized at ~$9.8k to stay inside the mandate — because the operating trends, margin expansion and cash generation support the valuation despite the China and regulatory overhangs.
